div.head: Ine 36
div.ab: LXXX. Se ðe ðeof gefehð, oððe him mon gefongenne agifð, ⁊ he hine þonne álæte, oððe þa ðiefðe gedierne, forgielde þone þeof his were.
LXXX. Se ðe þeof fehð, oþþe him mon gefongenne agifð, ⁊ he hine ðonne alæte, oþþe ða þyfðe gedirne, forgilde þone ðeof be his were.
Be ðeofes andfenge, ⁊ hine swa forlæte. Se ðe ðeof gefehð, oððe him mon gefongene agyfð, ⁊ he hine ðonne alæte, oððe ða þyfþe gedyrne, forgylde ðone ðeof be his were.
Qui furem ceperit, uel captum detinuerit (reddiderit) et ipsum dimiserit, uel furtum celauerit, reddat ipsum furem secundum weram eius (suam).
[Be ðeofes andfenge, ⁊ hine swa forlæte.] Se ðe þeof gefehð oððe him mon gefongenne agifð, ⁊ he hine þonne álæte, oððe þa ðiefðe gedierne, forgielde þone þeof [be] his were.
{LXXX} Se ðe ðeof gefehð oððe him mon gefongenne agifð, ⁊ he hine þonne álæte, oððe þa ðiefðe gedierne, forgielde þone þeof his were.
[Wenn] einer einen Dieb [bei der That] fängt, oder man ihm einen ertappten [zur Haft] übergiebt, und er ihn dennoch entlässt, oder den Diebstahl verbirgt, vergelte er den Dieb mit dessen Wergeld.

[If] someone catches a thief [in the act], or a thief who has been caught is handed over to him [for custody], and he nevertheless lets him go, or conceals the theft, let him pay for the thief with the latter’s wergeld.
He who captures a thief or has a captured thief given into his custody, and allows him to escape, or suppresses knowledge of the theft, shall pay for the thief according to his wergeld.
He who captures a thief, or is given a captured thief, and he then lets him get away, or conceals the theft, is to pay for that thief with his Wergild
He who catches a thief, or to whom [a thief] is entrusted as a prisoner, and then lets him go or conceals the theft, let him compensate by the wer of the thief.

Q i (Diebes Wergeld) scheint richtig laut des Objekts ‘Dieb’ (denn verschiedenen Ausdruck hat Ine zweimal, wo er für Begünstigung [s. d. Gl 2] vom Begünstiger fordert: ‘er löse sich durch sein eigen Wergeld’); ebenso wird der Dieb bezahlt II As 1, 1. 20, 8; þeofes wer II Cn 29 = Leis Wl 49. Später fordert auch hierfür des Freilassers Wergeld Q ii. Hn 12, 3

Q i (the thief's wergild) seems right in view of the object ‘thief’ (for Ine uses a different expression in the two places where, for harbouring [see that word in Gl 2], he demands of the harbourer: ‘let him redeem himself with his own wergild’); likewise the thief is paid for in II As 1, 1. 20, 8; þeofes wer II Cn 29 = Leis Wl 49. Later Q ii. Hn 12, 3 demand for this too the wergild of the man who released him
